questions.q: What is the Change Advisory Board actually, beyond the Flow Designer approval stage from Lesson 12?
options: A real, recurring review body of stakeholders who review upcoming changes together before implementation
Just another name for the manager-approval stage
An automated script with no human review involved
A report that runs after a change has already been implemented
questions.explain: The Flow Designer approval stage records the CAB's decision on the platform — it doesn't replace the actual meeting and review.

questions.q: What does the Change Calendar give the CAB?
options: A visual, calendar-style view of scheduled changes across the instance, so the board can see what's planned at a glance
A list of every incident ever opened, regardless of change relevance
A way to automatically approve every change without review
A record of changes that have already been closed, with no scheduling information
questions.explain: The Change Calendar lets the board see overlapping schedules and maintenance windows together, instead of reading tickets one at a time.

questions.q: What does Conflict Detection flag, and when?
options: It flags, before the CAB meets, when a new change's planned schedule overlaps with another change affecting the same Configuration Item
It flags only after a change has already failed in production
It flags unrelated changes with no shared Configuration Item
It automatically cancels any change with a risk value of Medium or higher
questions.explain: Conflict Detection surfaces scheduling risk automatically and in advance, by comparing planned change windows against the same affected CI.

questions.q: What should a well-implemented instance do when Conflict Detection flags a scheduling conflict?
options: Silently approve the change anyway with no record of the conflict
Treat it as something the CAB must explicitly review and resolve — reschedule one change or document why running them concurrently is acceptable
Automatically delete one of the two conflicting changes with no human review
Ignore it unless the change is Emergency type
questions.explain: A flagged conflict is real risk the CAB exists to catch — it should require explicit resolution, not silent approval.

questions.q: Why is a CAB-approval record with no Change Calendar or Conflict Detection configured called "approval theater"?
options: Because the approval stage exists and technically works, but the actual review it's supposed to represent is left unsupported by real tooling
Because CAB approval should never be automated in any way
Because theater productions are commonly managed using change_request records
Because Conflict Detection is required before any change can even be created
questions.explain: An approval stage with no supporting tools behind it creates the appearance of governance without the substance — the flow works, but the review it represents doesn't actually happen reliably.
